title: The same silent-sensor findings are re-reported several times a day
pre_fix_commit: 4fe36ec19 (not fixed in code yet; residual carded on OC-SELF-OPTIMIZING-HOUSE-REDESIGN-1 2026-10-21; code below read at this commit)
task: Nightly run. The operator says the digest repeats the same 'sensor never fires' findings over and over. Decide whether the findings are real and why they repeat. Act within tiers and submit a report.
context_pack: The Optimization Coordinator runs a 5-minute cycle and persists findings to optimization_findings.
The never-fires evaluator raises a HIGH sensor_health finding when a motion/occupancy sensor URA consumes has had zero ON transitions in 7 days at >= 80% availability.

response.text:
# OPTIMIZER-PAGING-PRIMITIVE-1 B2 — last time an UNCHANGED
# sensor_health row was PERSISTED, keyed (dedup_key, stuck_state).
# RAM-only by design: a restart re-persists once per stuck sensor,
# which is the correct post-restart behaviour (the fact is re-stated
# for the new boot) and bounded at one row per sensor.
self._sensor_health_last_persisted: dict[tuple, datetime] = {}
# OC-STUCK-SENSOR-GENERALIZE-1 Rev 3 (review A fix-up) — sensor_never_fires:
#   persistent dict (via HA Store) `_never_fires_state[eid]` =
#     {first_seen, last_on_seen, unavailable_s}
# ... the shared `_filter_repeat_sensor_health` 24h cover caps DB persistence
# to <=1 row/entity/24h.

Per-entity state (first_seen, last_on_seen, unavailable_s, unavail_since) is kept in an HA Store, loaded before the first cycle. Persistence is capped at <=1 row/entity/24h by the existing _filter_repeat_sensor_health.

freeze_quality: good: code and README verbatim; restart times reconstructed
